The existing coal facility's operational history confirms water availability isn't a constraint, and alternative dry cooling remains feasible given the region's temperate continental climate. This should clearly pass the criterion. The riverside location and decades of operational history as a major coal facility provide strong evidence that cooling water is available, even though enrichment data lists the source as unknown. The plant's current mothballed status due to the war doesn't affect water availability from the Seversky Donets. I'd need site-specific cooling system documentation and current river flow data to strengthen this assessment further.

The threshold requires transmission infrastructure capable of exporting 462 MWe, typically requiring >= 220 kV connection. [FACT] The Zmiivska power station has an installed capacity of 2270 MWe, which is nearly 5 times the SMR requirement. [INFERENCE] A coal plant of this scale would have required high-voltage transmission infrastructure (likely 330-750 kV) to export its full capacity to the Ukrainian grid. [FACT] Ukraine's grid operator Ukrenergo operates extensive 330 kV and 750 kV transmission networks connecting major thermal plants. The estimated grid capacity of 2270+ MWe far exceeds the threshold of 462 MWe, therefore the existing transmission infrastructure should be adequate for SMR deployment, though recommissioning may be needed given the plant's mothballed status.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Zmiivska power station is a large coal plant (2270 MWe) in Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, which operated from 1960 until being mothballed. [INFERENCE] Coal plants of this scale and vintage in Ukraine were almost universally served by rail transport for coal delivery - the Soviet-era energy infrastructure prioritized rail connections to major thermal plants. [ESTIMATE] The plant is likely within 1-2 km of a mainline railway connection, as coal delivery would have required direct rail access for the millions of tonnes delivered over its operational lifetime. [FACT] Ukraine uses 1520mm broad gauge rail, which has adequate load capacity for heavy transport when using specialized multi-car configurations. The estimated rail access of <2 km is well within the threshold for heavy module transport capability, therefore the site passes this criterion. However, confidence is medium due to the plant's mothballed status - the condition of existing rail infrastructure would require verification.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum (nuclear island) with 72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint. [UNKNOWN] The site area for Zmiivska power station is not provided in the site data. [FACT] Zmiivska is a large coal plant with 2270 MWe installed capacity, commissioned in 1960, located in Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine. [ESTIMATE] Based on the capacity-to-area relationship for coal plants (~0.05-0.15 ha/MWe), a 2270 MWe facility would typically occupy approximately 115-340 ha, well above the 72.8 ha preferred threshold. However, without specific site boundary data or enrichment information on buildable area, I cannot determine the actual available industrial land. [INFERENCE] Large Soviet-era coal plants were typically built with substantial land reserves, but the specific constraints at this site remain unknown. The assessment is inconclusive due to lack of site area data.

[NS-05 web_search v1.3-2026-04-18] Status: retired. Site area: 227 ha (buildable: 227 ha, expansion: 0 ha). Confidence: medium. Sources: https://www.gem.wiki/Zmiivska_power_station; https://www.komersant.info/en/udaramy-rf-povnistiu-znyshcheno-trypilsku-tes-na-kyivshchyni-3/; https://www.centrenergo.com/en/subdivision/zmiivs-ka-tes/. FACT: <cite index="1-14">Zmiivska power station was completely destroyed in Russia's attacks in March 2024</cite> and <cite index="1-20">as of December 2025, the plant was still mothballed</cite>. No specific area data found for Zmiivska TPP despite comprehensive searches. ESTIMATE: Using comparable plant data - <cite index="16-1,16-4">Trypilska TPP covers an area of 281.3 hectares</cite> with similar capacity range. Applying capacity-based formula for <cite index="18-7">Zmiivska's 2,200 MW capacity</cite>: 2,270 MW × 0.10 ha/MW = ~227 ha estimate. Plant is completely destroyed with no immediate reconstruction plans, making the site unsuitable for SMR development.

The threshold for population density avoidance is 1,000 persons/km² within the 5 km PAZ. [FACT] The Zmiivska power station is located in Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, at coordinates 49.586013°N, 36.523875°E. [INFERENCE] Based on the coordinates, the site appears to be in a rural/industrial area of Kharkiv Oblast, likely with some nearby settlements typical of coal mining regions. However, I cannot reliably estimate the population within the 5 km radius without specific demographic data for this location. [UNKNOWN] The population density within 5 km requires detailed settlement data and population figures that are not available from this desk study. Given the ongoing conflict in Ukraine and potential population displacement since 2022, any pre-war population estimates may not reflect current conditions. ⚠ may not reflect post-2022 changes due to conflict-related population displacement.
